newsitem.title: USA: Today's Man says not in talks with Men's Wearhouse.
newsitem.headline: Today's Man says not in talks with Men's Wearhouse.

text.p: Today's Man said Thursday that neither it nor its official creditor's committee is negotiating with Men's Wearhouse about a possible acquisition of Today's Man.
In a statement, the clothing retailer said it was flattered by Men's Wearhouse's interest.
But it said that Today's Man and its creditors' committee continue to negotiate and both parties fully anticipate finalizing and filing a consensual plan of reorganization in the near future.
In March, Today's Man, which is in bankruptcy proceedings, hired Salomon Bros., the Salomon Inc unit, to help obtain financing for a stand-alone plan of reorganization.
The company filed for bankruptcy protection in February 1996.

Men's Wearhouse disclosed its interest in acquiring more than a majority of Today's Man's 25 stores in a regulatory filing earlier in the day. The filing said it planned to sell up to 1.0 million common shares while a group of shareholders may sell up to 1.6 million shares, part of the proceeds of which it said it may use to fund the acquisition.
Today's Man estimated the possible acqusition at between $70 and $90 million.

It said in its filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission that its talks regarding a possible deal did not include Today's Man management and any understanding between it and Today's Man's creditors would likely be opposed by Today's Man.

"Due to the complexity of the situation and the conflicting goals of th several parties involved, there is a significant likelihood that the company may not be able to acquire the assets of Today's Man," Men's Wearhouse said in the filing.
